chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ibrahim, from Abi Ja'far, from 'Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abi Basir, who said:

“The diyah of a man is one hundred camels; if that is not available, then from cattle at the value of that; and if that is not available, then one thousand rams. This is in intentional killing, and in mistaken killing it is like intentional killing: one thousand mixed sheep.”
And the second possibility is that this is specific to the slave when he kills a free man intentionally; then in that case that becomes binding upon him, and that has indeed been narrated.

key_terms.الْإِبِلِ: camels, the primary measure of diyah in this report
key_terms.الْبَقَرِ: cattle given as an equivalent by value when camels are unavailable
key_terms.الْعَبْدِ: a slave, in the stated specific legal application
key_terms.دِيَةُ: financial compensation due for killing or bodily injury
key_terms.شَاةٍ مُخْلَطَةٍ: mixed sheep, meaning sheep of varied kinds or qualities in this context
key_terms.كَبْشٍ: a ram, listed here as an alternative form of payment

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about the diyah of a man in intentional and mistaken killing?
ai.summary: This report states the prescribed diyah for a man and lists substitute forms of payment when camels are unavailable. It also distinguishes between intentional and mistaken killing in the wording cited, then mentions another possible application specific to a slave who intentionally kills a free man.
